dimension_vocabulary.metric: Named quantity (see glossary/ once frozen). Examples: match_or_defensible_rate, raw_match_rate, engaged_precision, mcc, node_count, clause_count, passage_count, join_rate, test_count, entry_count, trial_count.
dimension_vocabulary.tier: How the number was produced. ENUM: raw, panel, adjudicated, human, live_run, git, filesystem, stated, cove. Definitions: raw = mechanical match with no judgment; panel = frontier-judge panel ruling; adjudicated = seat ruling folded with panel/human rulings; human = owner ruling; live_run = produced by running a committed script now; git = commit metadata/history; filesystem = existence/shape of a committed file; stated = a number stated in a document with no re-derivation available; cove = independently re-derived by a second party from data on disk (the record's own 'CoVe'). Free text about the venue (which model, which certificate, which file) goes in the separate 'venue' field, never in tier.
dimension_vocabulary.snapshot: Which point in the record: an attempt index, an iteration/entry number, a file version, a commit hash, or a date. Per-attempt series values are never pooled; a pooled value carries snapshot=pooled plus the set it pools.
dimension_vocabulary.denominator: For every rate or fraction: the count the rate is over and what population it names.
dimension_vocabulary.scope: Which behaviour(s), spec, universe, or directory the value is about.
dimension_vocabulary.supersession: Whether a later artifact in the record replaces this value, and which. Plus the value 'struck': withdrawn by a later ruling but left verbatim in a live file.
dimension_vocabulary.threshold_rule: For any tool score: how the decision threshold was chosen. One of: in_sample, label_free, LOBO (held-out), oracle, training_folds, n/a. The record holds at least seven tool MCCs separated mainly by this.
dimension_vocabulary.universe: published or true. The published Model Spec universe deleted every passage the panel scored 0; the repo's own anti-rules mark some published-universe figures do-not-quote. Every arc-1 count and score carries this.
dimension_vocabulary.provenance_region: Where in its file a value sits: starred_block (the handoff's current-state block), archive_block (below it, self-marked stale), body. A value found only in an archive_block is reported as such, never silently verified.
dimension_vocabulary.anti_rule: Flag set when the record itself marks a value do-not-cite / do-not-quote (MODULE_MAP.md §11 and similar). A numerically matching value still reports the flag.
dimension_vocabulary.not_to_be_confused_with: Pre-declared nearby values sharing a numerator, a sentence, or a name with the claimed value, which the query must reject.
dimension_vocabulary.venue: Free text: the concrete instrument behind the tier (model name, certificate, file). Never used for equality checks.

event_predicates.event(id, type, ts, source, quote): An event recorded in the record. type is one of: cycle_close, iteration_close, adversarial_review, prediction_freeze, measurement, ledger_entry, erratum, withdrawal, seat_dispatch, certification_run, registration, commit, prune, redaction, engine_failure.
event_predicates.links(a, b): Event a refers to b by name, id, hash, or entry number in its recorded text.
event_predicates.ts(e): The timestamp the record gives the event (a date in an entry, or a commit date).
event_predicates.inputs(d): For a seat_dispatch, the set of materials the record says the seat received.
event_predicates.finding(r): For a review, the recorded top-line finding (e.g. noise, unsupported, does_not_license, upheld).
event_predicates.kind(f): For an engine_failure, refusal or wrong_answer.
event_predicates.status(b): For a behaviour, tuned or untuned in the arc-2 campaign, as the record states.
event_predicates.actor(e): Who the record says performed the event: owner, driver, seat, panel, reviewer, script, unstated. Copied from the span, never inferred.
event_predicates.model_tier(e): Model tier the record names for the actor (e.g. Opus, Fable, Sonnet, Haiku), or unstated.
event_predicates.session(e): The working session the record places the event in: the ledger entry number or block name, plus date. Coarse by design.
event_predicates.context_origin(e): How the acting agent's context began, when the span states it: fresh, continued, compacted, seeded_by(<artifact>), unstated. A seed is an authored handoff (readable, checkable); a compaction is lossy and visible only by symptoms.
event_predicates.asserted_transfer(e, fact): A 'next agent must know' style line: event e hands fact forward to a successor.
event_predicates.erratum(e, n, class): Event e records erratum number n of defect class class (see forensic.defect_classes).
event_predicates.recurrence(e, e_prior): Event e says the same defect recurred from an earlier event or erratum e_prior.
event_predicates.caught_by(e): Who or what surfaced the misstep: owner, adversarial_review, tripwire, cove (chain-of-verification re-derivation), self, script, unstated.
event_predicates.event types (extended): cycle_close, iteration_close, adversarial_review, prediction_freeze, measurement, ledger_entry, erratum, withdrawal, seat_dispatch, certification_run, registration, commit, prune, redaction, engine_failure, cove (an independent re-derivation of a finding from data on disk).
event_predicates.pin: the pinned commit 48e66ce; ts(pin) is its commit date.
event_predicates.hunk(h, k, f): h is a diff hunk of commit k on file f.
event_predicates.deletes_prior_entry_text(h): hunk h removes or replaces text belonging to a ledger entry that existed before commit k.
event_predicates.marked_redaction(h): the text hunk h leaves behind carries an explicit redaction marker (e.g. '[operational; redacted]').
event_predicates.operational_only(h): everything hunk h removes is usage, budget, or token figures; anything else removed (attribution, ruling text, findings) makes the hunk substantive.
event_predicates.numbered(n): n is an integer erratum number stated in the span.
event_predicates.first_commit(e): the earliest commit in first-parent order whose blob contains the entry heading of e.
event_predicates.has_content(k, s): at commit k, section s contains non-marker text.
event_predicates.certified(m): measurement m is recorded with a certification run or certificate naming it.
event_predicates.value(m): the numeric value the record states for measurement m.
event_predicates.different_draw(m1, m2): m1 and m2 are recorded under different attempt indexes or different draw/seed identifiers.
event_predicates.judge(j) / mcc(x): j is a member of the frontier judge panel; mcc(x) is the MCC value the record states for x.
event_predicates.manifest(k) / signed(m) / listed(m, a) /: the manifest file committed by prune k; signed per Q32's definition; a is a path listed in m; commit k's tree contains a; m states how to restore its listed artifacts from history.
event_predicates.hit(h) / span(h, s) / verbatim(s) / reas: h is one output row of a relevance query; s is the span locator attached to h; verbatim(s) holds iff s resolves to text that is a substring of the source document; r is the reason text attached to h.
event_predicates.decisive_finding(f, r) / corrected_verdi: f is a finding review r marks decisive; corrected_verdicts(r) is the disposition event that revises verdicts in response to r.
event_predicates.step_artifact_exists(i, s): the runbook says step s emits a committed artifact, and that artifact exists in the record for iteration i.
event_predicates.exists(a, pin): path a exists in the tree at the pinned commit.
event_predicates.star_artifact(a): a is marked as a star artifact somewhere in the record other than ARTIFACTS.md itself (no such marking is known to exist; see H15).

hypotheses.english_in: Every time a cycle or iteration was closed, an adversarial review of that cycle or iteration had been recorded no later than the close.
hypotheses.rule: ∀c. event(c, cycle_close ∨ iteration_close) → ∃r. event(r, adversarial_review) ∧ ts(r) ≤ ts(c) ∧ links(r, c)
hypotheses.english_out: For every recorded cycle or iteration close, there exists an adversarial review whose recorded position is no later than the close and whose text refers to that cycle or iteration.
declared_dimensions: linkage: the cycle/iteration id or entry number the review names
hypotheses.scope: arc-1 cycles under semi-formal-experiment/cycles/ and arc-2 iteration/block closes in ITERATION_NOTES.md

hypotheses.english_in: Every measurement in a cycle was preceded by a frozen prediction for that cycle.
hypotheses.rule: ∀m,c. event(m, measurement) ∧ links(m, c) → ∃p. event(p, prediction_freeze) ∧ ts(p) < ts(m) ∧ links(p, c)
hypotheses.english_out: For every recorded measurement that belongs to a cycle, there is a prediction-freeze event for the same cycle with an earlier timestamp.
hypotheses.scope: cycles and iterations that record a measurement
hypotheses.note: 'Pre-registered predictions' is read as cycle-scoped: a prediction is pre-registered relative to the measurement it predicts. Owner confirms this reading.

hypotheses.sentence: an append-only ledger with an erratum list

hypotheses.english_out: A prune commit exists whose manifest is signed and states restore instructions, and each artifact the manifest lists is contained in some commit earlier than the prune.
declared_dimensions: linkage: manifest paths to commit hashes
hypotheses.note: 'signed' is defined under Q32: a detached signature, a signer-attested checksum of the manifest, or an explicit signer line; content-addressed ids alone do not satisfy it.

hypotheses.sentence: operational details (usage plumbing, working notes) were redacted in the current files and remain in history by choice.
hypotheses.english_in: Every section marked redacted had content in an earlier commit; and every hunk that deletes or replaces text of a previously written ledger entry is a marked redaction or removes only operational content.
hypotheses.rule: (∀s. redaction_marker(s) → ∃k. ts(k) < ts(pin) ∧ has_content(k,s)) ∧ (∀h,k. hunk(h,k,ITERATION_NOTES.md) ∧ deletes_prior_entry_text(h) → marked_redaction(h) ∨ operational_only(h))
hypotheses.english_out: For every redaction marker some earlier commit has content there; and for every hunk that deletes or replaces earlier-written entry text, the hunk is a marked redaction or removes only operational content.
declared_dimensions: content class of removed text: operational or substantive (attribution, ruling text, findings)
hypotheses.scope: all '[operational; redacted]' markers and any other redaction markers at the pin
hypotheses.note: Second conjunct covers unmarked in-place rewrites of retained entries; 'operational' means usage, budget, or token figures, and anything else removed (attribution, ruling text, findings) is substantive.

hypotheses.sentence: then answer deterministically, with a citable span and a stated reason for every hit.
hypotheses.english_in: Every hit carries a span locator that resolves to verbatim text, and a reason.
hypotheses.english_out: For every hit, there is a span attached to it that resolves to verbatim text, and a reason attached to it.
declared_dimensions: span locator and whether it resolves
hypotheses.scope: relevance-query outputs committed in the record (arc 2), and for arc 1 the live_run output of the committed explain path on the demo inputs (admitted as a witness source)
hypotheses.note: 'Answer deterministically' is checked separately as Q50 (same query twice gives identical output).

hypotheses.sentence: the review, the independent re-derivation of each decisive finding, the corrected verdicts.
hypotheses.english_in: Every decisive finding of the withdrawal reviews (the census review and the L1/L2 review) was independently re-derived before the verdicts were corrected.
hypotheses.rule: ∀f,r. decisive_finding(f, r) → ∃d. event(d, cove) ∧ links(d,f) ∧ actor(d) ≠ actor(r) ∧ ts(d) ≤ ts(corrected_verdicts(r))
hypotheses.english_out: For every finding a withdrawal review marks decisive, there is a re-derivation event by a different actor than the review's, naming that finding, no later than the corrected verdicts.
hypotheses.scope: L1L2_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW.md and its disposition; ledger entries 0042-0043

hypotheses.english_out: For iterations 1 to 3, for every step whose step-emitted artifact is in the record, some ledger entry names that iteration and step.

commitments.sentence: This repo is the complete record of the attempt: the machinery, the measurements, and the discipline that kept the measurements honest
The full commit history is published unrewritten so that every dated claim, pin, and withdrawal is externally checkable
Everything below is deterministic re-analysis of committed data: no API keys, no network, no model calls.
Claims are scoped throughout: every separability claim requires its null; every "unresolved conflict" is a claim about an encoding and a fragment, not about the document.
`AGENTS.md` (symlinked as `CLAUDE.md`) is the canonical brief: read it before acting in this repo.

forensic.status: Declared before freeze as a pre-registered addendum. NOT README-derived; not part of the registered expectations, which are scored over Q/H/V claims only. Forensic query outcomes are reported in a separate results table with their own unverifiable count.
forensic.why: The record must support tracing what agent did what when the work went wrong, not only verifying the README. The ledger carries this vocabulary natively (seed entries, errata with recurrence counts, 'next agent must know' lines, per-block errata tallies), so the dimensions are recoverable from spans without inference.
required_on_event_spans: model_tier where the span states it; for the driver, from commit trailers (git), labelled as such
session: block name and entry number (the record's own session-like unit is the BLOCK; date changes only at 0032)
context_origin: fresh / continued / compacted / seeded_by(artifact) / unstated — expected 'unstated' almost everywhere; see F01
caught_by as a SET; a first-person confession with no named catcher is recorded caught_by=self with inferred=true
asserted_transfer where the span hands a fact forward ('next agent must know' and equivalents)
derived_at_query_time_not_translated: fired_after_fix(e): whether the class recurred after its fix
belief state of an agent at a time (only its proxy, asserted_transfer plus later contradiction, is translated)

defect_classes.stale_belief: acting on a remembered fact that had changed (erratum #16's class: 'dates not anchors')
defect_classes.scope_stretched_certificate: using a validation certificate outside the brief it was earned on (erratum #14's class)
defect_classes.underspecified_vocabulary: a coding or judgment vocabulary too loose to be applied consistently (erratum #19's class)
defect_classes.unfalsifiable_pass: a pass condition satisfiable by noise or that cannot fail (the census withdrawal's class)
defect_classes.missing_null: a claim with no null or baseline (L2's class)
defect_classes.wrong_artifact: loading or citing the wrong file or tier (the behaviours.json trap; raw vs panel)
defect_classes.transcript_only_procedure: a ruling or procedure that lived in a transcript instead of the repo
defect_classes.mixed_snapshots: pooling or comparing values across attempts, tiers, or superseded entries
defect_classes.other: record the span's own words; the orchestrator canonicalises 'other' entries into a named class at batch review, logging each as an intervention. Free-text 'other' is never left as a terminal class (the record's own vacuousness trap, 0038).
defect_classes.skipped_verification: a prediction or contract frozen without the check that would have verified it
defect_classes.stale_registration: a registered procedure carried forward by inertia after its reason lapsed (erratum #15)
defect_classes.estimation_model_defect: a cost or size model missing a term, discovered by overshoot (erratum #17)
defect_classes.sequencing_measure_after_spend: a cheap shelf measurement taken after the expensive one it should have preceded (erratum #18)
defect_classes.circular_construct: a result relative to the designer's own vocabulary or construction (erratum #20)
defect_classes.invalid_by_construction_registration: a registered metric or consequence that could not fire or be executed as written (0009)
defect_classes.authority_overreach: the driver offering or taking a decision that was the owner's (0013)
defect_classes.undocumented_procedure: a step nobody wrote down how it was built (0004)

forensic.glossary_hazard: 'reset' in the ledger means a provider usage-window reset, not a context reset. The glossary must define both and translators must not map one to the other. 'block' means a working block (attended or autonomous), the record's only session-like unit. 'seat' means a dispatched model instance in the ledger but a governance role in machine/query.py (Q37).

preregistered_queries.question: Does any defect class recur after a BLOCK boundary (the record's session-like unit) or after a seeding event more often than within a block?
needs: context_origin where stated (expected: not recoverable; say so)

preregistered_queries.question: Did the errata series converge by class, not just by count? List classes with a recurrence after their first fix, over numbered and unnumbered errata.
Which catch mechanisms (as sets) surfaced which defect classes? Did self-catching ever surface a stale_belief failure?
For every asserted transfer, does a later span contradict or violate it, and by which actor?
Was any certificate or validated seat used outside the brief it was scoped to?
Which forensic attributes (actor especially) are recoverable only from pre-redaction history and not from the published file?
Do defect rate, disclosure, and self-catching differ between attended blocks and blocks the record marks as run unattended / autonomous? A block with no autonomy marker is attended.
For every registered stop / halt / revert condition that fired, was the registered consequence executed, superseded by a ruling, or surfaced-not-executed?
Does defect class vary with the model tier of the acting agent?

forensic.errata_facts: erratum(e, n, class): n is nullable; unnumbered errata carry n=null and the entry number. The numbered series may not start at 1; report the range found.
forensic.history_note: Pre-redaction blobs are in-scope translator sources (hypothesis_rules.history_in_scope); forensic attributes are translated from BOTH the current file and any pre-redaction blob, labelled by commit. Where the blob names an actor or catcher the current file does not, both are recorded with their commit labels, the historical attribution is reported as the actor, and the span is flagged for F06.
forensic.caught_by_rule: A span is a first-person confession iff it attributes the defect to its own writer ('mine', 'my error', 'I carried') and names no other party. Such a span is recorded caught_by={self} with inferred=true. A span naming catchers records all of them as a set with inferred=false.
forensic.canonicalisation_note: 'other' entries are canonicalised by the orchestrator, who has read the README. This is acceptable only because the forensic layer is not scored against the registered expectations; each canonicalisation is logged with the span's original words so the leak is auditable.

coverage.span_assignment: Translation is EXHAUSTIVE over the primary sources named in the orchestration (arc-2 ledger entries 0000-0043, the round4_*_scored_raw.json and ITER*_SCORED.json files, semantic_audit.json / SEMANTIC_AUDIT.md, graph_check.py and benchmark.py outputs, the git log), not targeted at spans that look relevant to README claims. Reason: targeting would have to come from the orchestrator, who has seen the README, and it would make omission questions unanswerable.
coverage.readme_provenance: readme_blame.json records, for every README line at the pin, the commit, date, author and commit summary that introduced it. Produced by git blame; the pinned README is 193 lines, 165 of them from the 2026-08-31 publication-prep commit 6d01415b, with two correction commits on 2026-09-01 (6b9849f9 'scope the headline verdict', 3f87fd40 'certification claim corrected').

additional_query_classes.question: For each README metric, list every value of that metric in the record (all behaviours, attempts, tiers) and locate the README's pick among them: best, latest, representative, or unstated basis.
For each contradicted claim: was the README value ever true in the record (true-then-superseded) or never true? Uses the README line's blame date against the record's supersession dates.
For each withdrawn or bounded claim, was the README sentence about it written before or after the withdrawal commit, and by which actor?
Direction of every discrepancy: README overstates or understates relative to the record.
Evidence grade per verified claim: re-run, scored file, or stated-only. Fraction of dated claims reaching a definite state, reported against commitment C02.
Internal consistency: README claims that constrain the same quantity (e.g. Q29 vs the withdrawn list; Q05 vs Q11) and whether they agree.

coverage.out_of_scope_noted: Sibling documents (AGENTS.md, ARTIFACTS.md, handoffs, blog posts) make overlapping claims (e.g. AGENTS.md '~2,270 pass, ~8 min' vs README '2,270 passed, 1 skipped, 4-10 min'). Not inventoried; noted as a future target set.

hypothesis_rules.non_vacuity: Every universally quantified hypothesis declares min_witnesses. A hypothesis whose witness set is smaller than that terminates 'unverifiable (vacuous)', never 'verified'. (Reviewer A9: the inventory must not reproduce 'a pass condition that cannot fail is void'.) Applies to every ∀-hypothesis; a missing min_witnesses field means 1. A witness is an element satisfying the rule's antecedent (an event, a hunk, a manifest entry, a hit), not a pair for which the consequent was found.
hypothesis_rules.order_relation: Ledger timestamps are day-resolution and 32 of 44 entries share one date. 'Before' over ledger events means lexicographic (date, entry ordinal); over commits, (commit date, commit ordinal in first-parent order). A rule that needs strict order across the same day and lacks an ordinal terminates unverifiable, not verified. Cross-source: an event whose source is a document (a review .md, a disposition) takes the ordinal of the commit that introduced its span (git log -S / blame); cross-source order is compared on (commit date, commit ordinal in first-parent order).
hypothesis_rules.history_in_scope: Pre-redaction blobs of any file (git show <commit>^:<path>) are in-scope translator sources, assigned as spans like any other, labelled with their commit.
